html:
The Worrorran languages are a small family of Aboriginal Australian languages from the northwest Kimberley in Western Australia, a rugged land of sandstone ranges, gorges and a broken coast between King Sound and the King Edward River.

They are not part of the Pama-Nyungan family that covers most of Australia. Like many northern languages, they mark nouns by class and pack much meaning into prefixes on the verb. Linguists usually group them in three branches:

  • Worrorra in the west, with languages such as Unggumi and Umiida.
  • Ngarinyin in the east.
  • Wunambal in the north, with dialects such as Gaambera and Miwa; Kwini is close to them.

Their speakers share a law and ritual life tied to the Wandjina, the rain and creator spirits painted in the region's rock shelters. All the Worrorran languages are now endangered, with few fluent speakers left, and communities are working to record and teach them. See also Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Worrorran languages are a small family of Aboriginal Australian languages from the northwest Kimberley in Western Australia, a rugged land of sandstone ranges, gorges and a broken coast between King Sound and the King Edward River.
